title: Purity of the determinant line
statement:
Let $X_0$ be a normal geometrically connected curve over $k_0$, let
$\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$, and let $\mathcal V$ be an
irreducible lisse Weil sheaf of rank $r$ on $X_0$. Then there is
exactly one real number $a$ such that the
determinant line
$\det(\mathcal V)$ is
punctually $\iota$-pure of weight
$a$.

proof.text: Choose a geometric base point of $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$. Use the fundamental representation of [def-wf-fundamental-representation], which is continuous by [lem-wf-weil-fundamental-representation]. Its finite coefficient field can be chosen as follows. By [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves], the underlying lisse $\Qlb$-sheaf is represented by a lisse $E$-sheaf for some finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Choose an $E$-basis of its fibre. The degree-one Weil operator $T_s$ in [def-wf-fundamental-representation] and its inverse have finitely many matrix entries in $\Qlb$. Enlarge $E$ to contain these entries; this remains finite over $\mathbf Q_\ell$. The conjugation identity for $T_s$ and the geometric action holds over this $E$, since it holds after the injective scalar extension to $\Qlb$. Consequently the formula $\rho(\gamma s^n)=\rho_{\rm geom}(\gamma)T_s^n$ gives the same Weil representation over $E$. By [cor-galois-lisse-representations](2), the lisse $E$-model gives a continuous $E$-representation of $\pi_1(X,\bar x)$ on its fibre, and the equivalence commutes with scalar extension to $\Qlb$; hence $\rho_{\rm geom}$ is this $E$-representation extended to $V$, and in the chosen $E$-basis it takes values in $\operatorname{GL}_r(E)$. Since $T_s^{\pm1}$ also has entries in $E$, $\rho$ takes values in $\operatorname{GL}_r(E)$, and it is continuous by [lem-wf-weil-fundamental-representation] ($E$ carries the subspace topology of $\Qlb$). Thus it is a continuous $E$-representation.

By [def-mg-determinant-line], $\mathcal L=\det(\mathcal V)$ is the rank-one lisse Weil sheaf with character $\chi=\det\circho:W(X_0)	o E^	imes$. This character is continuous: in the chosen finite basis its value is the determinant polynomial in the matrix entries of $ho$; the inverse is obtained by applying that polynomial to $ho(g^{-1})$. The curve in the statement is normal and geometrically connected by hypothesis, and by [def-pc-curve] it is integral, separated and of finite type over $k_0$ and of dimension one, hence irreducible and pure of dimension one; the coefficient convention of [def-weil-punctual-weights] has $\ell
e p$, hence $\ell
mid q$. Therefore [thm-wf-rank-one-finite-geometric-image-curve] applies to $\chi$ and gives finite geometric image. Now [cor-wf-rank-one-punctual-purity-curve], for this same character and the restriction of the fixed $\iota$ to $E$, says that $\mathcal L$ is punctually $\iota$-pure of the real weight $a=2\log_q|\iota(c)|$, where $c=\chi(s)
e0$. This proves existence in exactly the punctual-purity convention of [def-weil-punctual-weights].

There is a closed point $y$ of $X_0$. Indeed $X_0$ is nonempty by geometric connectedness in [def-weil-geometric-hypotheses], and quasi-compact because its structure morphism is of finite type ([def-weil-finite-type-morphism]). Its topology is Kolmogorov: distinct points in an affine chart are distinct prime ideals and are distinguished by a basic open $D(f)$ ([def-weil-affine-spectrum]); if two points have no common affine chart, any affine neighborhood of the first omits the second. Hence [lem-sc-quasi-compact-kolmogorov-closed-point] applies to $X_0$. By [lem-kun-closed-point-field](a), $\kappa(y)$ is finite over $k_0$, so it is a finite field with cardinality $q_y>1$.

source.place: proof, second paragraph: existence of a closed point

proof.text: Suppose $a$ and $a'$ are both punctual purity weights of $\mathcal L$. By [def-mg-determinant-line] its stalk at the point chosen in step 3 is one-dimensional. The local operator $F_y$ of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace] is a composite of isomorphisms (point transport, pullback comparisons and the iterated Weil isomorphism). In a basis $v\ne0$ write $F_y(v)=\alpha v$; invertibility gives $\alpha\ne0$. The two purity conditions in [def-weil-punctual-weights] give $q_y^{a/2}=|\iota(\alpha)|=q_y^{a'/2}$. Taking real logarithms gives $(a/2)\log q_y=(a'/2)\log q_y$. Since $q_y>1$, $\log q_y>0$, so $a=a'$. Together with step 2 this proves exactly one real purity weight. This argument uses only that the determinant has rank one; irreducibility is not needed for this particular conclusion.
